common.date-mask: Placeholder showing the expected date format. TRANSLATE THIS: the order of day, month and year differs by locale, so a French user should see jj/mm/aaaa and a German one tt.mm.jjjj. Keep the same number of characters per part.
common.dismiss: Dismiss button on a notification. A VERB, imperative. Slightly more formal than OK; both are used and both are translated once.
common.email-example: Placeholder in an email field. An EXAMPLE ADDRESS — translate the local part and the company word if that reads more naturally in the target language, and keep it a valid address.
common.lock.already-locked: User-facing notification: "Document already locked by another user, please refresh your page." Shown when the user pressed Lock but another user locked the document first (HTTP 409). Says what happened and what to do. Used by document detail and collection detail.
common.lock.lock-no-permission: User-facing notification: "You don't have permission to lock this document." Shown when the server refuses a lock for lack of permission (HTTP 403). A STATEMENT about the user's rights.
common.lock.locked-by: Tooltip on the lock control of a locked document. {{ owner }} is the username holding the lock; {{ date }} is the day it was locked, already formatted for the user's locale (e.g. "October 9, 2026"). Keep both placeholders; reorder them as the language needs.
common.lock.locked-by-another-user: User-facing notification: "You can't unlock this document because it is locked by another user." Shown when the server refuses an unlock because someone else holds the lock (HTTP 409).
common.lock.unlock-no-permission: User-facing notification: "You don't have permission to unlock this document." Shown when the server refuses an unlock for lack of permission (HTTP 403). A STATEMENT about the user's rights.
common.ok: Dismiss button on a notification. An ACKNOWLEDGEMENT, and the shortest form the language allows. Used by every snackbar that offers one, so it is translated once.
common.page-number: Current page indicator with no known total. A NOUN plus a number.
common.page-of: Current page out of a known total. Both are numbers; word order may differ in the target language.
common.permission-denied: Shown when the server refuses an action for lack of permission. A STATEMENT about the user's rights, not an error in the system. Used across features, so it is translated once.
common.search-deleted: Confirms a saved search was removed. {{ name }} is the user's own content.
common.search-saved: Confirms a saved search was stored. {{ name }} is the name the user gave it, so it is their own content and never translated.
common.search-updated: Confirms a saved search was renamed or changed. {{ name }} is the user's own content.
common.select-item: Accessible name of the checkbox that selects one row in a document list. An IMPERATIVE instruction; `{{ name }}` is the document's own title and is NOT translated. Announced by a screen reader, never shown. Place the placeholder wherever the target language needs it.
common.tag-added: Confirms a tag was applied to a document. {{ name }} is the tag text, entered by a user.
common.tag-applied: Confirms a tag was applied from the document detail page. {{ name }} is the tag text.
confirm.add-a-permission: Title of the dialog that grants a permission on a saved search. A VERB phrase, imperative.
confirm.delete: Confirm button on a destructive dialog. A VERB, imperative, and the shortest form the target language allows — it sits next to Cancel. Used by every delete confirmation in the application, so it is translated once.
confirm.delete-collection: Title of the dialog confirming deletion of a collection. A collection groups documents; deleting it does not delete them.
confirm.delete-collection-question: Message of the collection-delete confirmation. A QUESTION.
confirm.delete-comment: Title of the confirmation dialog shown before deleting a comment on a document. Title case follows the other confirmation dialog titles.
confirm.delete-comment-question: Question in the confirmation dialog before deleting a comment on a document. The user answers with the Delete or Cancel button.
confirm.delete-document: Title of the dialog confirming a soft delete of one document from its detail page.
confirm.delete-document-named: Message of the document soft-delete confirmation. {{ name }} is the DOCUMENT TITLE, repository content. A QUESTION seeking confirmation.
confirm.delete-document-question: Message of the soft-delete confirmation. A QUESTION seeking confirmation; keep it a question in the target language.
confirm.delete-group: Title of the dialog confirming deletion of a group, in administration.
confirm.delete-group-named: Message of the group-delete confirmation. {{ name }} is the GROUP NAME, server data, never translated. A QUESTION — keep the quotation marks the target language uses, and move the placeholder if word order requires it.
confirm.delete-reply: Title of the confirmation dialog shown before deleting a reply to a comment on a document. Title case follows the other confirmation dialog titles.
confirm.delete-reply-question: Question in the confirmation dialog before deleting a reply to a comment. The user answers with the Delete or Cancel button.
confirm.delete-saved-search: Title of the dialog confirming deletion of a saved search — a stored query, not any document.
confirm.delete-saved-search-named: Message of the saved-search delete confirmation. {{ name }} is the search the user named, so it is their own content and is never translated.
confirm.delete-selected-documents: Message of the BULK soft-delete dialog. {{ count }} is always 2 or more — the singular case uses confirm.delete-the-document instead, so this string never needs an "(s)" suffix and should read naturally as a plural.
confirm.delete-the-document: Message of the soft-delete dialog when the document has no usable title. A QUESTION. The definite article is deliberate: one specific document, unnamed here.
confirm.delete-user: Title of the dialog confirming deletion of a user account, in administration.
confirm.delete-user-named: Message of the user-delete confirmation. {{ name }} is the USERNAME, server data. Two sentences: a QUESTION then a WARNING; the second is the only place the user is told the action is irreversible.
confirm.delete-vocabulary-entry: Title of the dialog confirming deletion of one entry from a Nuxeo vocabulary (a controlled list of values).
confirm.delete-vocabulary-entry-named: Message of the vocabulary-entry delete confirmation. {{ name }} is the entry id and {{ directory }} the vocabulary name — both server data. Two placeholders, and their order may need to change in the target language.
confirm.got-it: Dismiss button on an informational dialog that asks for no decision. An ACKNOWLEDGEMENT, informal; not a confirmation of an action.
confirm.move-named-to-trash: Message of the soft-delete dialog when the document has a title. {{ name }} is the document name — keep the quotation marks the target language uses, and move the placeholder if word order requires it. A QUESTION.
confirm.move-to-trash: Title of the dialog confirming a SOFT delete. "Trash" is the recoverable area, so the wording must not imply permanence — contrast confirm.permanently-delete-document.
confirm.permanently-delete-document: Title of the dialog confirming an IRREVERSIBLE delete of one document. "Permanently" is the load-bearing word and must survive translation.
confirm.permanently-delete-documents: Title of the dialog confirming an IRREVERSIBLE delete of several documents. Plural.
confirm.permanently-delete-documents-cou: Message of the BULK irreversible-delete confirmation. {{ count }} is always 2 or more — the singular case uses confirm.permanently-delete-warning instead, so this should read naturally as a plural and never needs an "(s)" suffix.
confirm.permanently-delete-warning: Message of the irreversible-delete dialog. Two sentences: a QUESTION then a WARNING. Both matter — the second is the only place the user is told the action cannot be reversed.
confirm.update: Title of the dialog that edits an existing permission. A VERB, imperative.
contracts.sample-document-title: A made-up document name used by the contracts showcase. SAMPLE DATA — translate the word "Contract" if the example reads better that way, and leave the code and extension alone.
contracts.saved-search-placeholder: Example text in the saved-search name box on the contracts page. An EXAMPLE, so translate it into something a speaker of the target language would plausibly type — "Q3" is a fiscal quarter and "Contracts Pending Review" is a state, neither is a product term.
contracts.showcase-dialog-message: Explanatory body of the showcase dialog. `@nuxeo-satori/platform/ui` is a PACKAGE NAME and must not be translated.
contracts.showcase-dialog-title: Title of a demonstration dialog on the contracts showcase page. DEMO copy, not a product feature.

document-detail.message.ke-category-not-: Error shown when AI classification answered with a category name that is not in the configured list. {{ category }} is the name the AI returned, shown verbatim; {{ count }} is how many categories exist. Knowledge Enrichment is a Hyland AI service (product name, do not translate) that analyses a document's file and proposes metadata. login.skip-link: Link at the top of the sign-in page that moves keyboard focus to the username field, bypassing decorative chrome. WCAG bypass-block link; a verb phrase.
login.title: Page heading on the sign-in screen. A verb phrase: authenticate to the application. Use the product's 'log in' wording consistently with nav.sign-out's 'sign out'.
nav.clipboard.aria-label-many: Accessible name for the Clipboard navigation item when it holds MORE THAN ONE item. `{{ name }}` is the already-translated nav label ("Clipboard") and `{{ count }}` is the number, always 2 or greater here — the item is hidden entirely when the clipboard is empty, so this text is never shown for zero. The clipboard is an in-application staging area for copy/move, not the operating system clipboard. Plural counterpart of nav.clipboard.aria-label-one. If the target language needs more than two plural forms for this, say so rather than forcing it into two.
nav.clipboard.aria-label-one: Accessible name for the Clipboard navigation item when it holds exactly ONE item. `{{ name }}` is the already-translated nav label ("Clipboard") and `{{ count }}` is the number, always 1 here. The clipboard is an in-application staging area for copy/move, not the operating system clipboard. Singular counterpart of nav.clipboard.aria-label-many; if the target language needs more than two plural forms for this, say so rather than forcing it into two.
nav.clipboard.copy: Button copying the clipboard's documents into the current folder. A VERB, imperative.
nav.clipboard.empty: Shown when the clipboard holds no items. The clipboard is an in-application staging area for copy/move, not the operating system clipboard.
nav.clipboard.hint: Instruction shown beneath nav.clipboard.empty. The quoted phrase "Add to Clipboard" is a menu item label the user will look for, so it must match the translation of that menu item exactly, and keep the quotation marks.
nav.clipboard.move: Button moving the clipboard's documents into the current folder. A VERB, imperative.
nav.clipboard.remove: Accessible name and tooltip on the button that takes one item out of the clipboard. A verb phrase.
nav.clipboard.tip: Guidance shown when the clipboard has items. 'Container' means a folder or other document that can hold children. 'Paste or move' are two distinct operations.
nav.collections.empty: Shown when the user has no collections. A 'collection' is a user-curated set of documents, a Nuxeo domain term.
nav.expired.empty: Shown when no documents have passed their expiry date. 'Expired' refers to a document retention/expiry date, not a session.
nav.favorites.empty: Shown when the user has marked no documents as favorites. 'Yet' implies the list can be filled, and is worth preserving.
nav.favorites.hint: Instruction shown beneath nav.favorites.empty explaining how to add one. 'Star icon' refers to a ★ button on each document row.
nav.favorites.remove: Accessible name and tooltip on the button that unmarks one document as a favorite. A verb phrase.
nav.folders.empty: Shown in place of the folder tree when the repository has no folders the user may see. Note it may mean 'none exist' or 'none visible to you'; prefer neutral phrasing.
nav.item.administration: Navigation entry for the admin area: users, groups, vocabularies, audit. A noun naming a section.
nav.item.assets: Navigation entry for digital assets - images, video, rich media. A noun, plural. Domain term: 'asset' here means a media file, not a financial asset.
nav.item.browse: Navigation entry for the folder tree and document list. A VERB, imperative - 'browse the repository', not the noun 'a browse'.
nav.item.browse-adf-hx: Navigation entry for the folder tree and document list. A VERB, imperative - 'browse the repository', not the noun 'a browse'. Customer-facing. The 'adf-hx' in the key is an internal library name that must not appear in the translation; translate it the same way as nav.item.browse.
nav.item.clipboard: Navigation entry for the in-application staging area used for copy and move. NOT the operating system clipboard; if the target language distinguishes them, use the application sense.
nav.item.collections: Navigation entry for user-curated sets of documents. A noun, plural. Nuxeo domain term: a 'collection' is a named set a user assembles.
nav.item.dashboard: Navigation entry for the landing page of summary cards. A noun naming the page.
nav.item.expired-queue: Navigation entry listing documents past their retention expiry date. 'Expired' refers to a document retention date, not a session or a licence. 'Queue' is a worklist.
nav.item.favorites: Navigation entry for documents the user has starred. A noun, plural. US spelling in the source; use the target language's own convention.
nav.item.knowledge-discovery: Navigation entry for the Knowledge Discovery page. Knowledge Discovery is Hyland's AI product that answers questions about the repository's documents and cites its sources (product name, do not translate).
nav.item.personal-space: Navigation entry for the user's own workspace folder. A noun phrase naming a place.
nav.item.recently-viewed: Navigation entry for the list of documents this user opened. An adjectival phrase describing the documents, not an instruction.
nav.item.search-filters: Navigation entry opening the saved-search and filter panel. 'Search' is a NOUN qualifying 'filters' - filters for searching, not an instruction to search for filters.
nav.item.settings: Top-level navigation item, and the accessible name of its drawer toggle. A NOUN naming the section.
nav.item.tasks: Navigation entry for workflow tasks awaiting this user. A noun, plural.
nav.item.trash: Navigation entry for deleted documents pending permanent removal. A noun naming a place, recoverable - not 'rubbish' or 'waste'.
nav.loading: Accessible name on a progress spinner, announced to screen readers while a navigation panel fetches data. A present participle describing an in-progress state.
nav.recent.empty: Shown when the user has not viewed any documents yet. 'Recently viewed' is a history of documents this user opened.
nav.refresh: Accessible name and tooltip on a small icon button that reloads one panel of the navigation drawer. A verb, imperative.
nav.sign-out: Button that ends the user's session. A verb, imperative. Note this is 'sign out', not 'log out' — keep the product's wording consistent with the sign-in screen.
nav.tasks.dashboard: Link to the full tasks page. 'Dashboard' is the name of that page. A verb phrase: 'view the tasks dashboard'.
nav.tasks.empty: Shown when the user has no workflow tasks awaiting action. 'Pending' means awaiting the user's action.
nav.tasks.retry: Button shown after the task list fails to load, which re-attempts the request. A verb, imperative.
nav.tree.retry: Button re-attempting a failed load of the personal space tree. A VERB, imperative.
nav.tree.root: Button returning the folder tree to the repository root. A NOUN.
nav.tree.toggle: Accessible name for the chevron button that expands or collapses one folder in the navigation tree. A VERB phrase, imperative. `{{ name }}` is the folder's own title and is NOT translated — place it wherever the target language needs it, which is the whole reason it is a parameter rather than appended to the end.
note-format.html: Note body format in the note editor's format list. Value `text/html`. HTML = HyperText Markup Language, the code web pages are written in; keep the acronym.
note-format.markdown: Note body format, shown in the note editor's format dropdown. HTML, XML and Markdown are format names and must NOT be translated; 'Text' must. Value `text/markdown`.
note-format.plain: Note body format, shown in the note editor's format dropdown. HTML, XML and Markdown are format names and must NOT be translated; 'Text' must. Value `text/plain`.
note-format.xml: Note body format in the note editor's format list. Value `text/xml`. XML = Extensible Markup Language, a structured text format; keep the acronym.

permissions.right.AddChildren: Shown in the Right column of a document/collection permission table. (The permission PICKER uses a separate `permission.*` key set, so this text does not appear there.) This is a Nuxeo access right, NOT a file-system permission. The key leaf is the server-side permission identifier and must not be translated; only the value is. Create documents inside this folder. "Children" means contained documents, not people.
permissions.right.Everything: Shown in the Right column of a document/collection permission table. (The permission PICKER uses a separate `permission.*` key set, so this text does not appear there.) This is a Nuxeo access right, NOT a file-system permission. The key leaf is the server-side permission identifier and must not be translated; only the value is. Means full control, including managing other users' permissions. A NOUN phrase.
permissions.right.ManageWorkflows: Shown in the Right column of a document/collection permission table. (The permission PICKER uses a separate `permission.*` key set, so this text does not appear there.) This is a Nuxeo access right, NOT a file-system permission. The key leaf is the server-side permission identifier and must not be translated; only the value is. Start and administer workflows (multi-step review/approval processes) on this document.
permissions.right.Read: Shown in the Right column of a document/collection permission table. (The permission PICKER uses a separate `permission.*` key set, so this text does not appear there.) This is a Nuxeo access right, NOT a file-system permission. The key leaf is the server-side permission identifier and must not be translated; only the value is. View the document but not change it. A VERB in English; a noun form is fine if that reads better.
permissions.right.ReadCanCollect: Shown in the Right column of a document/collection permission table. (The permission PICKER uses a separate `permission.*` key set, so this text does not appear there.) This is a Nuxeo access right, NOT a file-system permission. The key leaf is the server-side permission identifier and must not be translated; only the value is. Read plus add the document to a collection. "Collect" refers to Nuxeo Collections, a user-defined grouping of documents.
permissions.right.ReadRemove: Shown in the Right column of a document/collection permission table. (The permission PICKER uses a separate `permission.*` key set, so this text does not appear there.) This is a Nuxeo access right, NOT a file-system permission. The key leaf is the server-side permission identifier and must not be translated; only the value is. Read plus delete, but not modify. The ampersand joins two rights and can become the target language's own conjunction.
permissions.right.ReadWrite: Shown in the Right column of a document/collection permission table. (The permission PICKER uses a separate `permission.*` key set, so this text does not appear there.) This is a Nuxeo access right, NOT a file-system permission. The key leaf is the server-side permission identifier and must not be translated; only the value is. Nuxeo calls this right "ReadWrite" but it is shown as "Edit" deliberately, because that is what it means to a user: read plus modify. A VERB in English; use whatever part of speech reads naturally as a table cell.
permissions.right.Remove: Shown in the Right column of a document/collection permission table. (The permission PICKER uses a separate `permission.*` key set, so this text does not appear there.) This is a Nuxeo access right, NOT a file-system permission. The key leaf is the server-side permission identifier and must not be translated; only the value is. Means delete the document. A VERB in English; a noun form is fine if that reads better as a table cell.
permissions.right.Write: Shown in the Right column of a document/collection permission table. (The permission PICKER uses a separate `permission.*` key set, so this text does not appear there.) This is a Nuxeo access right, NOT a file-system permission. The key leaf is the server-side permission identifier and must not be translated; only the value is. Modify the document. A VERB in English; a noun form is fine if that reads better.

shared.add-tag: Accessible name for a suggested-tag button that adds that tag when clicked. A VERB, imperative. `{{ name }}` is the suggested tag and is not translated.
shared.content-lake.bulk-ingest-failed: Error shown when the server refused the request to send documents to Content Lake and gave no reason. 'Bulk ingest' is the server job that sends documents to Content Lake (product name, do not translate).
shared.content-lake.ingest-stalled: Error for an administrator when a job sending documents to Content Lake stopped making progress. {{ commandId }} is the job's technical identifier, {{ state }} its last server status (a technical word such as RUNNING, shown verbatim), {{ processed }} how many documents were done and {{ total }} how many there were. Content Lake, Nuxeo and HxAI are product names (do not translate).
shared.content-lake.ingest-stalled-unkno: Same as shared.content-lake.ingest-stalled, used when the server did not say how many documents the job covers; 'unknown' stands in for that total. {{ commandId }} is the job's technical identifier, {{ state }} its last server status shown verbatim, {{ processed }} how many documents were done. Content Lake, Nuxeo and HxAI are product names (do not translate).
shared.content-lake.no-command-id: Error shown (on a document page or in the Upload to Content Lake dialog) when the server accepted a request to send documents to Content Lake but did not return the identifier needed to follow its progress. 'Bulk ingest' is the server job that sends documents to Content Lake; 'command id' is that job's technical identifier.
shared.include-file: Accessible name for the checkbox that includes one file in an import. A VERB, imperative — it selects the file rather than describing it. `{{ name }}` is the filename and is not translated.
shared.remove-group: Accessible name for the button removing one group chip from a user. A VERB, imperative. `{{ name }}` is the group name and is not translated.
shared.remove-item: Accessible name for the button that removes one selected value — a chip — from a multi-select field or an upload list. A VERB, imperative. `{{ name }}` is the value shown on the chip and is not translated; place it where the target language needs it. ONE key for every such button in the application: the string and its context are identical everywhere, so a translator should see it once.
shared.remove-tag: Accessible name for the button removing one tag chip. A VERB, imperative. `{{ name }}` is the tag text and is not translated. One key for every such button — the string is identical across browse, document detail and the adf-hx details panel.
shared.view-citation: Accessible name for the inline marker opening a cited source in an AI answer. A VERB, imperative. `{{ number }}` is the citation ORDINAL shown in the answer, a digit, not translated.
shell.ai.clear: Accessible name for the button that empties the conversation history. A verb phrase: 'clear the chat'. It discards the conversation; it does not close the panel.
shell.ai.close: Accessible name for the button that closes the assistant panel. A verb phrase. It keeps the conversation; contrast with shell.ai.clear.
shell.ai.empty-state: Shown in the AI assistant panel before the first message. A full SENTENCE listing what the assistant can do. ACRONYM: 'AI' means Artificial Intelligence. Expand or transliterate it according to the target language's convention for that term, as shell.ai.open does.
shell.ai.heading: Heading in the assistant panel's empty state. PRODUCT NAME — do not translate 'Nuxeo'. ACRONYM: 'AI' means Artificial Intelligence. Expand or transliterate it according to the target language's convention for that term, as shell.ai.open does.
shell.ai.input-placeholder: Placeholder in the assistant's message box, inviting a free-text question. 'Your documents' means the documents this user can see. The trailing '...' is deliberate and informal.
shell.ai.open: Accessible name for the header button that opens the assistant panel. ACRONYM: 'AI' means Artificial Intelligence. Expand or transliterate it according to the target language's convention for that term.
shell.ai.send: Accessible name for the button that submits the typed message to the assistant. A verb phrase, imperative.
shell.ai.sources: Heading above the documents an AI answer cited. A NOUN, plural — the documents the answer came from, not a menu of options.
shell.ai.suggestion.modified-today: A suggested question offered as a button in the AI assistant panel. A full QUESTION the user is inviting the assistant to answer; keep it a natural question in the target language rather than translating word for word.
shell.ai.suggestion.recent-uploads: A suggested question offered as a button in the AI assistant panel. An IMPERATIVE instruction to the assistant.
shell.ai.suggestion.summarize-tasks: A suggested question offered as a button in the AI assistant panel. An IMPERATIVE instruction to the assistant.
shell.ai.title: Title in the assistant panel's header bar. ACRONYM: 'AI' means Artificial Intelligence. Same term as shell.ai.open; keep the two consistent.
shell.due: Word shown in the navigation drawer's task list before the due fragment ('in 3 days'); the other state reads 'Overdue'. Adjective meaning 'due'; not a noun.
shell.expired-on: Marks a document whose retention expired. {{ date }} is an already-formatted date, so do not add your own.
shell.file: Rendered from an Angular binding in app-shell.component.html — usually one branch of a two-state control, so its opposite is a sibling key. Keep it as short as the English.
shell.last-modified-on: Shows when a collection last changed. {{ date }} is already formatted.
shell.menu.about: Item in the account menu opening product information. A PREPOSITION used as a heading, as English menus do; use whatever the target language uses for an 'About this product' entry.
shell.menu.ai-features: Account-menu item toggling AI features, showing the current state. ACRONYM: 'AI' means Artificial Intelligence. Expand or transliterate it according to the target language's convention for that term, as shell.ai.open does. `{{ state }}` is the translated word for On or Off; place it wherever the target language needs it.
shell.menu.help: Item in the account menu. A NOUN naming the destination.
shell.menu.state-off: The disabled state of a toggle, shown inside the AI Features menu item. An ADJECTIVE or short word, not a verb.
shell.menu.state-on: The enabled state of a toggle, shown inside the AI Features menu item. An ADJECTIVE or short word, not a verb.
shell.menu.themes: Item in the account menu opening the theme picker. A NOUN, plural.
shell.off: Rendered from an Angular binding in app-shell.component.html — usually one branch of a two-state control, so its opposite is a sibling key. Keep it as short as the English.
shell.overdue: Rendered from an Angular binding in nav-drawer.component.html — usually one branch of a two-state control, so its opposite is a sibling key. Keep it as short as the English.
shell.search.no-results: Shown in the search results dropdown when a query matched nothing.
shell.search.placeholder: Visible label text for the header global search field (associated <label>, not placeholder-only naming). Lists the three kinds of thing the search covers; keep the commas and 'or' as a readable list of alternatives.
shell.search.searching: Transient status shown in the search results dropdown while a query runs. The trailing ellipsis character (…) indicates work in progress and should be kept.
shell.settings.menu: Accessible name for the header button that opens the settings menu. A noun phrase naming the menu, not an instruction.
shell.slot-empty: Empty state for an extension slot with nothing registered. {{ name }} is the slot or item label — already translated before it arrives here.
shell.task-due.by-days-many: Shown in the Tasks panel of the left navigation drawer, directly after the separate word 'Due' (shell.due) or 'Overdue' (shell.overdue), which is rendered in its own styled span — so this text must read naturally after that word. Follows 'Overdue'; the due date passed {{ count }} whole days ago (2 or more). One of a singular/plural pair chosen in code by count === 1; languages with more plural forms (for example Polish) will need real plural rules later.
shell.task-due.by-days-one: Shown in the Tasks panel of the left navigation drawer, directly after the separate word 'Due' (shell.due) or 'Overdue' (shell.overdue), which is rendered in its own styled span — so this text must read naturally after that word. Follows 'Overdue'; the due date passed one day ago. {{ count }} is always 1 here. One of a singular/plural pair chosen in code by count === 1; languages with more plural forms (for example Polish) will need real plural rules later.
shell.task-due.by-hours-many: Shown in the Tasks panel of the left navigation drawer, directly after the separate word 'Due' (shell.due) or 'Overdue' (shell.overdue), which is rendered in its own styled span — so this text must read naturally after that word. Follows 'Overdue'; the due date passed {{ count }} hours ago (always 2 to 23). English has no singular case here; languages with several plural forms will need plural rules later.
shell.task-due.by-less-than-an-hour: Shown in the Tasks panel of the left navigation drawer, directly after the separate word 'Due' (shell.due) or 'Overdue' (shell.overdue), which is rendered in its own styled span — so this text must read naturally after that word. Follows 'Overdue'; the due date passed within the last hour or two.
shell.task-due.in-days-many: Shown in the Tasks panel of the left navigation drawer, directly after the separate word 'Due' (shell.due) or 'Overdue' (shell.overdue), which is rendered in its own styled span — so this text must read naturally after that word. Follows 'Due'; the task is due in {{ count }} whole days (2 or more). One of a singular/plural pair chosen in code by count === 1; languages with more plural forms (for example Polish) will need real plural rules later.
shell.task-due.in-days-one: Shown in the Tasks panel of the left navigation drawer, directly after the separate word 'Due' (shell.due) or 'Overdue' (shell.overdue), which is rendered in its own styled span — so this text must read naturally after that word. Follows 'Due'; the task is due one day from now. {{ count }} is always 1 here. One of a singular/plural pair chosen in code by count === 1; languages with more plural forms (for example Polish) will need real plural rules later.
shell.task-due.in-hours-many: Shown in the Tasks panel of the left navigation drawer, directly after the separate word 'Due' (shell.due) or 'Overdue' (shell.overdue), which is rendered in its own styled span — so this text must read naturally after that word. Follows 'Due'; the task is due in {{ count }} hours (always 2 to 23). English has no singular case here because under two hours reads 'in less than an hour'; languages with several plural forms will need plural rules later.
shell.task-due.in-less-than-an-hour: Shown in the Tasks panel of the left navigation drawer, directly after the separate word 'Due' (shell.due) or 'Overdue' (shell.overdue), which is rendered in its own styled span — so this text must read naturally after that word. Follows 'Due'; the task is due within the next hour or two.
shell.test.platform-nav-item: Label on a platform nav list item in a unit-test host template only. Not shown in the product UI; uses the same word as the real Browse nav entry for focus-ring contrast tests.
shell.test.personal-space-nav-item: Label on the Personal Space nav list item in a unit-test host template only. Not shown in the product UI; matches the real Personal Space sidebar entry for NXENG-778 focus-visible tests.
shell.test.clipboard-nav-item: Label on the Clipboard nav list item in a unit-test host template only. Not shown in the product UI; matches the real Clipboard sidebar entry for NXENG-873 focus-visible tests.
tab.tabs-ai-insights: Tab label on the document page for the AI Insights panel. Noun phrase naming the panel. Descriptor id `app.tabs.aiInsights`. AI = artificial intelligence; use the abbreviation usual in your language.
tab.tabs-annotations: Tab label on the document detail page. A NOUN naming the panel it opens. Descriptor id `app.tabs.annotations`.
tab.tabs-history: Tab label on the document detail page. A NOUN naming the panel it opens. Descriptor id `app.tabs.history`.
tab.tabs-permissions: Tab label on the document detail page. A NOUN naming the panel it opens. Descriptor id `app.tabs.permissions`.
tab.tabs-publishing: Tab label on the document detail page. A NOUN naming the panel it opens. Descriptor id `app.tabs.publishing`.
tab.tabs-view: Tab label on the document detail page. A NOUN naming the panel it opens. Descriptor id `app.tabs.view`.
tasks.document: Rendered from an Angular binding in tasks-page.component.html — usually one branch of a two-state control, so its opposite is a sibling key. Keep it as short as the English.
tasks.due-label.due-in-days-many: Shown in the task details panel of the Tasks page, next to the task's due date. The task is due in {{ count }} whole days (2 or more). One of a singular/plural pair chosen in code by count === 1; languages with more plural forms (for example Polish) will need real plural rules later.
tasks.due-label.due-in-days-one: Shown in the task details panel of the Tasks page, next to the task's due date. tasks.due-label.due-in-hours-many: Shown in the task details panel of the Tasks page, next to the task's due date. ui.update: Button in the shared edit dialogs (collection and saved-search sharing). Verb, imperative: saves the changes to an existing entry; the same button reads 'Create' for a new one — not the noun 'an update'.
app.preset.badge: Short badge in the application header, shown only on a presales demonstration server, naming the demo configuration currently applied. {{ label }} is that configuration's display name, usually a prospect's company name, and is not translated. A 'preset' here is a named set of demonstration settings.
